Robyn Speer must be credited as Robyn Speer, the name used on her academic
work. The wordfreq software is distributed under Apache License 2.0; see
wordfreq-LICENSE.txt.

wordfreq includes data that may be redistributed under Creative Commons
Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0:
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/

Its combined frequency estimates use data derived from sources including:

- Google Books Ngrams and Google Books Syntactic Ngrams;
- the Leeds Internet Corpus;
- Wikipedia;
- ParaCrawl;
- OPUS OpenSubtitles 2018, with attribution to OpenSubtitles;
- SUBTLEX word lists created by Marc Brysbaert and collaborators;
- aggregate word statistics collected from Twitter.

The upstream project states that the SUBTLEX authors must be credited and that
SUBTLEX remains freely available data:
https://www.ugent.be/pp/experimentele-psychologie/en/research/documents/subtlexus

KeySwitchFix transformation
---------------------------

KeySwitchFix does not embed the wordfreq package or its original word lists.
tools/generate_blooms.py reads the pinned English and Persian frequency data,
normalizes/filter words that the supported keyboard layouts can produce, and
stores only probabilistic Bloom membership bits plus a compact table of
physical-key collision priors. The common, frequent, common-prefix Bloom files
and collision-prior table derived from wordfreq are distributed under CC
BY-SA 4.0. Application source code remains under the project MIT license.

Pinned wordfreq files:

- wordfreq/data/large_en.msgpack.gz
  SHA-256 dffae8066b78dce0a6667cf5f58e567054f902674667090a7ac8a8a44628b05c
- wordfreq/data/small_fa.msgpack.gz
  SHA-256 bfb503f6b0d6bdddce720ee8154faf1c79d8b0417e6c865643da3b17b7638057
